newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court upholds $2 bln for alleged Marcos victims.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court upholds $2 bln for alleged Marcos victims.

text.p: An appeals court in California on Tuesday upheld an award of nearly $2 billion to thousands of alleged victims of the late Philippine dictator Ferdinand Marcos.

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, in a written ruling released in San Francisco, said that Marcos could be held liable for the alleged human rights abuses, and affirmed the massive 1994 jury award to his victims.
In 1994, a federal jury in a class action civil rights suit in Hawaii awarded $1.9 billion to some 9,500 victims and family members of victims who suffered at the hands of Marcos's government.

The Honolulu jury found that Marcos, who died there in exile in 1989, was responsible for major human rights abuses, including torture, murder and the "disappearances" of Filipinos during his rule that ended in 1986.
An attorney for the Marcos estate in Washington was not immediately available to comment Tuesday.

Lawyers for the alleged victims of Philippine human rights violations said Tuesday's appeals court decision was a major victory that could help them to collect assets of the Marcos estate held in Swiss bank accounts and elsewhere.

"It's fantastic," attorney Sherry Broder in Honolulu said of the decision. "I'm very pleased for the victims, many of whom have been waiting over 20 years for justice. Now that we have the judgment affirmed, we'll be able to continue our efforts to collect."
Various rival groups have staked claims to Marcos monies in Switzerland at Swiss Bank Corp and Credit Suisse. The two have an estimated $475 million deposited by the late dictator Marcos.

The Marcos accounts in Switzerland were frozen by Swiss authorities in 1986 at the request of the Philippines government. The Philippines government has also claimed the Swiss funds, alleging they were stolen from government coffers.
